transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I’m Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist here. What brings you in today?

Well, hello Doctor. Thank you for seeing me. I... well, I came in because I just can't seem to get anything in order anymore. It's really getting out of hand. Like my kitchen table, for instance. It is completely covered with my husband's appointment papers. He's been having such trouble with his sciatica lately, and the doctors keep sending these confusing summaries. I told him he needs to ask them to print the instructions larger because his reading glasses are ancient, but he never listens. 

But anyway, the table is just buried in his papers, and all these church flyers—oh, Pastor Dave is retiring next month, which is a real shame because his wife plays the organ so beautifully, we're really going to miss her at the Easter service—and then there's all my notes from the senior center, and just... half-finished lists I write for myself everywhere. I just sit down at that table, looking at the piles, and I don't know which thing to do first. I just sit there trying to figure it out, and then... well, the whole day is just gone. I don't even know where the time goes.
Have you been feeling down, sad, or have you lost interest in things you used to enjoy?

Sad? Oh, no, I wouldn't say that. I don't feel down or anything. I still want to do the things I love, like my watercolor painting. I just got this beautiful new set of brushes, actually. My daughter ordered them for me off the internet—from Amazon, I think? It’s amazing what they can just drop at your door these days. The delivery driver, a very nice young man, always leaves the packages right behind the big potted fern on the front porch so they don't get wet. 

Which reminds me, I really need to water that fern. It's been so dry this week, hasn't it? The weather report said we might get rain on Tuesday, but you can never really trust the meteorologists on Channel 4. They said it would snow on Thanksgiving three years ago and we didn't get a single flake, which was fine by me because my sister was driving up from Ohio and her tires were practically bald... 

Wait, what did you ask me? I'm sorry, I completely lost my train of thought.
Do you ever find yourself bothered by thoughts that you can’t seem to get out of your head, or do you feel like you have to do certain things over and over again to make yourself feel better?

Thoughts stuck in my head? No, I wouldn't say that. And I don't really do things over and over to make myself feel better. I mean, unless you count wiping down the kitchen counters, because my husband always leaves breadcrumbs everywhere when he makes his sandwiches. He just loves that thick sourdough from the bakery downtown. 

You know, the bakery that used to be owned by the Miller family? I think they sold it last year to a nice young couple from out of state. They brought in all these fancy new pastries, like those little French macarons. I actually tried to make macarons myself once for my book club. We were reading a lovely novel set in Paris—oh, what was the title? The cover had a little bicycle on it... Anyway, my macarons were a complete disaster. The recipe said you have to be so precise with the baking time, but my oven always runs a bit hot. I’ve been meaning to call the repairman about that oven for months now. He’s the same man who fixed our washing machine when it started making that awful clanking noise during the spin cycle. He told me I was putting too many towels in at once, but how else are you supposed to get all the laundry done on a Sunday? 

I'm sorry, what were we talking about? Did you ask me about my laundry?
Do you often find yourself struggling to stay focused on tasks, even when you know they’re important, or do you have trouble organizing your day?

Yes, exactly! That’s really what I was trying to say when I first sat down. I just can't seem to get anything in order anymore. It's like I was telling you with my kitchen table being completely covered in my husband’s appointment papers and the church flyers and my notes from the senior center... 

Oh, the senior center is actually hosting a bingo night next Friday to raise money for the animal shelter. They always have the best prizes. Last year my friend Martha won a beautiful woven basket full of local jams and jellies. Her grandson ate all the strawberry jam in one single weekend! He’s a growing boy, though, plays football for the high school. They have a very good team this year, their uniforms are a lovely shade of maroon, which is so much nicer than the bright orange the next town over wears. It just clashes terribly with the green field... 

But anyway, what was I... right, organizing my day. Yes, I have all these half-finished lists I write for myself mixed in with all those papers on the table, and I know I need to focus on them because they're important, but I just sit there staring at the mess. I don't know which thing to do first, so I just sit there trying to figure it out, and before I know it, the whole day is just gone.
When did you first start having trouble with staying focused and getting organized like this? Was it something that started when you were a child or has it been more recent as an adult?

Well, you know, even as a little girl I had this trouble. My mother kept all my old report cards in this beautiful cedar chest at the foot of her bed... oh, that chest smelled so wonderful, I think my sister has it now. But anyway, my teachers always wrote the exact same thing on them. They said I was a bright girl, but just so careless. I was always forgetting my reading books and my homework. They constantly had to remind me to finish my seatwork before they would let me go outside for recess. 

Recess was my absolute favorite part of the day, though. We had this enormous oak tree at the edge of the playground at Lincoln Elementary. My best friend Sally and I used to try and collect the acorns to make little families out of them, drawing tiny faces on the shells. Sally actually fell out of a lower branch of that tree in the third grade and broke her collarbone. Her mother was frantic, just absolutely frantic. She was a very nervous woman, Mrs. Higgins. But oh, she made the most wonderful homemade lemonade in the summers. She’d squeeze the lemons by hand, none of that powdered stuff you get nowadays. 

Have you seen the price of lemons at the grocery store lately, by the way? It’s just highway robbery! I went to buy some for a lemon pound cake last week, and I nearly fell over right there in the produce aisle. The produce manager, a very tall man with thick glasses, he told me it was because of some freeze down in Florida, or maybe it was California, I can't quite recall. He said the citrus crops were just devastated...

I'm sorry, I've done it again, haven't I? What was the question? Were you asking about my grocery shopping?
Would you say these difficulties with staying focused and getting organized have caused you significant problems in your daily life, like at home, with family, or in managing your responsibilities?

Oh, yes, it really has. It’s been just awful lately. I actually had to give up leading this big event we were planning at the senior center because I just couldn't keep the catering and the volunteer lists straight. It was going to be a beautiful spring luncheon, too. We were planning a Hawaiian luau theme, and I even bought this lovely floral lei from a little party store on Main Street. The woman who works there, Brenda, she has the most beautiful garden at her house. She grows these massive, prize-winning tomatoes every summer. I tried to grow tomatoes once, but the squirrels kept taking bites out of them right before they were ripe. They are such a nuisance, those squirrels! They completely ruined my wooden bird feeder last winter. My husband tried to put a metal baffle on the pole, but those little acrobats just figured a way around it anyway...

Wait, what was I saying? Oh, right, my responsibilities. Yes, well, it's gotten so bad that my daughter has actually started coming over to double-check my bills and my appointments. She told me she just can't trust that I can keep everything straight on my own anymore. It's a bit humiliating, really, having your own child hover over your mail. But she’s always been so good with paperwork, just like her father. He used to do all our taxes at the dining room table with this heavy old adding machine that made the most satisfying clicking sound. I wonder whatever happened to that machine? I think we might have donated it to the rummage sale at the Methodist church. They have a wonderful rummage sale every October. I bought a beautiful vintage tea set there a few years ago. The teapot has a tiny chip on the spout, but you can barely see it if you turn it toward the wall...

I'm sorry, I've lost the thread again. Did you ask me about the tea set?
